record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For projective billiards in smooth convex planar domains, where the reflection law preserves the tangential component of velocity and reverses the component along a prescribed transverse line field, which projective billiards possess an invariant symplectic form and admit a variational description?

evidence.quote: Which ones have invariant symplectic forms and variational description?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth convex planar domain with boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a smooth line field defined along $\partial\Omega$ that is transverse to $\partial\Omega$ at every point. The associated projective billiard map acts on the space of oriented lines meeting $\Omega$ as follows: when an oriented line hits $\partial\Omega$ at a point $p$, it is reflected into a new oriented line through $p$ determined by the rule that the component of the direction vector tangent to $\partial\Omega$ at $p$ is preserved, while the component along the prescribed transverse line $\mathcal{L}(p)$ is reversed. (When $\mathcal{L}$ is the inward normal field, this reduces to the standard billiard reflection law.)

Characterize, among all such pairs $(\partial\Omega, \mathcal{L})$, those projective billiards which:
(a) admit an invariant symplectic form on the phase space of oriented lines (equivalently, on a suitable open subset of $T^*\partial\Omega$); and
(b) admit a variational (generating-function) description, i.e., trajectories arise as critical points of some functional on chains of boundary points.

Give a complete geometric description of the line fields $\mathcal{L}$ (and corresponding boundaries) for which (a) and/or (b) hold.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. Partial progress exists in the special case of Hamiltonian projective billiards (e.g., billiards bounded by a sphere with an exact transverse field, where an invariant symplectic form is induced by the hyperbolic metric), but a full characterization in the planar convex setting has not been established.
